class electrip.config.json_model.JsonModel(locos=None, server=None, joystick=None, sound=None)[source]¶
Object-tree representing all the data needed by Electrip.
Able to load and save itself from/to Json-files.

Stores several attribute-lists, which are lists of tuples of the form [("attribute_name", default_value), ...]. Each attribute-list maps to an object in the configuration:

  • self.loco_attributes -> Loco
  • self.engine_attributes -> Engine
  • self.event_sound_attributes -> EventSound
  • self.function_sound_attributes -> FunctionSound
  • self.segment_attributes -> SoundSegment
  • self.function_attributes -> Function
  • self.server_attributes -> Server
  • self.joystick_attributes -> Joystick
  • self.sound_attributes -> Sound

The Object-tree looks similar to this:

JsonModel
    |
    |- locos
    |     |- Loco
    |     |    |- name = "V 200"
    |     |    |- image = "/home/user/V200.png"
    |     |    |- engine = ...
    |     |    |- ...
    |     |
    |     |- Loco
    |     |    |- ...
    |     |- ...
    |
    |- server
    |     |- host = "localhost"
    |     |- port = 4303
    |     |- ...
    |
    |- joystick
    |     |- emergency_button = 0
    |     |- accel_axis = 2
    |     |- ...
    |- ...
add_file_to_zip(zip_file, file_path, dest='')[source]¶

Adds a file located at file_path to zip-file, placing it at the subdirectory dest. Example:

self.add_file_to_zip(self,
                     zip_file,
                     "/home/user/image.gif")
self.add_file_to_zip(self,
                     zip_file,
                     "/home/user/test.wav",
                     "sound")
# Will place 'image.gif' in the root
# directory of zip_file and 'test.wav' in the
# subdirectory '/sound'
add_files_to_zip(zip_file, config_object, attribs, dest='')[source]¶

Adds multiple files to zip_file, where attribs is a list of attributes of config_object which should be used for the file locations. See add_file_to_zip(). Example:

self.add_files_to_zip(self,
                      zip_file,
                      segment,
                      ["load_sound",
                       "accel_sound",
                       "decel_sound",
                       "idle_sound"])
# Will add the files located at
# segment.load_sound, segment.accel_sound, ...
# to 'zip_file'
create_copy()[source]¶

Returns a new JsonModel-instance, whose object-tree is identical, except that it is a recursive copy of the existing one. This means, that the new instance and the original one don’t share any objects, only the tree-structure and the values of the objects attributes. This allows the control_ui module to modify its own copy of the configuration without destroying the original one.

create_dict(config_object, attribute_list)¶

Returns a dictionary-representation of config_object, using the attributes from attribute_list. attribute_list is a list of tuples of the form [("attribute_name", default_value), ...]. The default values are not used in this method.

create_loco(loco_obj, wrapper, unsaved_changes_method)[source]¶

This method covers the logic to create a new Loco-object. Depending on the situation, one may want to use different data-types for this operation. This is specified by wrapper, which must be one of DictWrapper or ObjectWrapper. E.g. if you want to create a new Loco using an existing Loco, you could do this:

new_loco = self.create_loco(existing_loco,
                            ObjectWrapper,
                            self.unsaved_changes)

unsaved_changes_method defines the method to be called if an attribute on the new loco changes, usually this is Config.unsaved_changes.

Returns: The new Loco

create_loco_dict(loco)[source]¶

Returns a dictionary-representation of the object-tree in loco. This is needed save the loco in the Json-format.

static get_param_list_from_dict(config_dict, attribute_list, ignore=False)[source]¶

Uses a dictionary config_dict and attribute_list to create a parameter-list which can be fed into a constructor of an object. attribute_list is a list of tuples of the form [("attribute_name", default_value), ...]. The default values are used, if config_dict has no key for the respective attribute_name. If the ignore flag is set to false (default) a warning is printed if a fallback to default values happens.

Example: You could create a new Server-object like this:

server_dict = {"host": "localhost",
               "port": 4303}
server = Server(self.unsaved_changes,
                *self.get_param_list_from_dict(server_dict,
                                               self.server_attributes),
                True)
# 'server_dict' doesn't contain all needed keys, so the
# default-values in self.server_attributes will be used
static get_param_list_from_object(obj, attribute_list, unused_ignore=False)[source]¶

Uses an object obj and attribute_list to create a parameter-list which can be fed into a constructor of a new object. Works similar to get_param_list_from_dict()

static get_utf8_bytestring(value)[source]¶

Returns a utf8-bytestring made from a unicode-object value. If value is not a unicode-object, value is returned.

load(file_path)[source]¶

Loads the object-tree from a Json-file specified by file_path.

load_loco(file_path)[source]¶

Returns a Loco-object which is unpacked from a zip-file-package. See save_loco().

save(file_path)[source]¶

Saves the current object-tree to the Json-file specified by file_path.

save_loco(loco, dir_path)[source]¶

Exports loco to a zip-file, including all sound- and image-files needed. This standalone package is placed in dir_path, named like loco.name.

save_opened_file(file_path)[source]¶

Stores the file_path of the currently opened file in last_file.json which will be placed in the current working directory.

set_absolute_path(path_prefix, config_object, attribs)[source]¶

Appends path_prefix to all attributes in the list attribs of config_object. Used to change a relative path to an absolute path.

unsaved_changes(obj, name, value)[source]¶

To be called whenever an action changes the JsonModel-object. Normally this is done using UnsavedChangesHandler.

linear_segment_function Module¶

class electrip.config.linear_segment_function.LinearSegmentFunction[source]¶

Function consisting of linear segments which build a continuous line connecting certain control points. The function increases monotonically.

add_control_point(x, y)[source]¶

Adds a control point at (x, y), updating the function. If the resulting function after inserting (x, y) would not be monotonically increasing, nothing will happen.

calc_func_segment(point1, point2)[source]¶

Solves the equation y=a*x+b using the two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2). Returns (a, b).

get_segment_nr_from_x(x)[source]¶

Returns the number of the function segment belonging to the x-coordinate x.

get_segment_nr_from_y(y)[source]¶

Returns the number of the function segment belonging to the y-coordinate y.

get_x(y)[source]¶

Returns the functions x-value matching y. (Possible due to the functions injectivity).

get_y(x)[source]¶

Returns the functions y-value at x.

load(control_points)[source]¶

Loads the function from the control points, building the linear function segments between the control-points. control_points are a list of (x, y)-point-tuples defining the control-points of the function.

move_control_point(nr, x, y)[source]¶

Moves the nr-th control point to the point (x, y). If x > x of the next point, nothing will happen, to ensure a monotonic increase (Same for y > y of next point).

remove_control_point(nr)[source]¶

Removes the nr-th control point from the function. Attempting to delete the first or last control point will result in nothing happening, because they are necessary for the function to exist.

class electrip.config.loco_functions.ToggleMode[source]¶

Class used to specify different ways to toggle a button:

  • SWITCH: first click = on, second click = off
  • PUSH: button pressed = on, button released = off
  • PUSH_LIMITED: button pressed = on, button released = off, program may turn off earlier
  • TAP: first click = on, program decides when off
PUSH = 1¶
PUSH_LIMITED = 2¶
SWITCH = 0¶
TAP = 3¶

sound_engines Module¶

class electrip.config.sound_engines.DieselEngine(save_status_method, start_sound=None, idle_sound=None, quit_sound=None, sound_segments=None, event_sounds=None)[source]¶

Bases: electrip.config.sound_engines.Engine

A Diesel-powered engine. It has start_sound, idle_sound and quit_sound attributes, which are strings containing the path to the sound-files representing the off-on-transition, idle-state and on-off-transition of the engine. For sound_segments and event_sounds see Engine.

class electrip.config.sound_engines.Engine(save_status_method, sound_segments, event_sounds)[source]¶

Bases: electrip.config.unsaved_changes.UnsavedChangesHandler

Abstract representation of an engine which has some kind of sound. sound_segments is a list of SoundSegment- objects defining the sound of the engine at different speed-ranges. event_sounds is a list of EventSound- objects defining sounds which should be played under certain conditions.

class electrip.config.sound_engines.EngineType[source]¶

Defines all possible engine types for sound generation.

  • STEAM: A steam engine
  • DIESEL: A diesel engine
DIESEL = 'diesel'¶
STEAM = 'steam'¶
class electrip.config.sound_engines.SteamEngine(save_status_method, idle_sound=None, cylinder_steam_sound=None, nr_strokes=4, stroke_start_delay=2.0, wheel_diameter=1.2, min_freq=0.2, sound_segments=None, event_sounds=None)[source]¶

Bases: electrip.config.sound_engines.Engine

A steam-powered engine.
Args:
  • idle_sound: sound which is played continuously, base noise of a steam-engine
  • cylinder_steam_sound: sound which is played when the engine starts to move, simulating steam coming out of the cylinder
  • nr_strokes: the number of cylinder strokes the engine performs (typically 4 on a 2 cylinder engine)
  • stroke_start_delay: the timespan the cylinder_steam_sound is played before the first stroke sound is played
  • wheel_diameter: diameter of the traction wheels
  • min_freq: minimal frequency of strokes / second, helps to avoid extremely long pauses between strokes at speeds near 0
  • sound_segments: see Engine
  • event_sounds: see Engine

A Function consisting of SoundSegment- objects, used to determine the sound to be played at a certain speed.

Returns the number of the SoundSegment belonging to the x-coordinate x.

get_sound(x, sound_type)[source]¶

Returns the sound of type sound_type from the segment at position x. Example:

func = SoundFunction(various_diesel_sound_segments)
sound = func.get_sound(67.0, "load_sound")

# 'sound' now stores the filepath to
# the "load_sound" of the segment at 67.0 km/h

sound_segments Module¶

class electrip.config.sound_segments.DieselSoundSegment(save_status_method, start, end, load_sound=None, idle_sound=None, accel_sound=None, decel_sound=None)[source]¶

Bases: electrip.config.sound_segments.SoundSegment

A segment for Diesel-sound. Provides different sounds for different conditions:

  • load_sound: engine is running under load at constant speed
  • idle_sound: engine is running idle at constant speed
  • accel_sound: engine is accelerating
  • accel_sound: engine is decelerating
set_position(position)[source]¶

Creates the idle_sound-attribute if position is SegmentPosition.MIDDLE, erases it if position is SegmentPosition.UPPER (in the upper DieselSoundSegment the loco is always under load).

class electrip.config.sound_segments.SegmentPosition[source]¶

Defines two types of Segments: upper and middle ones. Used e.g. in SoundSegment.set_position().

MIDDLE = 1¶
UPPER = 2¶

Defines sounds for a certain speed-range reaching from speeds greater than start to speeds smaller or equal to end.

set_position()¶

Allows segment-implementations to react to position-changes. Should be called whenever the position of a segment changes.

class electrip.config.sound_segments.SteamSoundSegment(save_status_method, start, end, stroke_sounds=None)[source]¶

Bases: electrip.config.sound_segments.SoundSegment

A segment for steam-sound. Provides the attribute stroke_sounds, which is a list of strings specifying the sound-filepaths for the cylinder-strokes. E.g.:

segment = SteamSoundSegment(some_method,
                            12.0,
                            31.2,
                            ["/home/user/tchoo.wav",
                             "/home/user/piff.wav",
                             "/home/user/paff.wav"])
# if active, tchoo-piff-paff-tchoo-piff-paff-tchoo...
# should be played

will create a new SteamSoundSegment reaching from any speed greater than 12.0 km/h to 31.2 km/h. If active, tchoo.wav, piff.wav and paff.wav. should be used as cylinder-stroke-sounds.

set_position(position)[source]¶

Does nothing at all, position doesn’t matter for SteamSoundSegment.
